benchmark_metadata.task_prompt: Fix company inference so configured keywords match whole alphanumeric words instead of substrings. Matching must be case-insensitive. In multiword keywords, punctuation, whitespace, and underscores may separate words. For example, `rapid` must not match `api`, while `HACKER-RANK` must match `hacker rank`. Preserve the existing keyword weights, scoring thresholds, tie behavior, configured keywords, and all unrelated triage behavior.

tool_calls.note: Counts only tool calls during the without-PRISM task phase (steps 28-42). Setup was shared.

content_consumed.note: Setup (config.py + agent.py full reads) was shared between runs. In a truly isolated run, the without-PRISM agent would consume ~39196 chars of source code.

token_usage.note: Server-side API token usage metrics are not exposed in the local agent transcript. These counts require API-level metering infrastructure.

tool_calls.note: Counts only tool calls during the with-PRISM task phase (steps 45-56).

files_read: No direct source file reads needed

prism_index_cost.note: PRISM indexing is fully deterministic and local — zero LLM tokens consumed.

prism_context_cost.note: Token estimates use chars/4 approximation (PRISM convention). PRISM CLI was used directly rather than prompt hook in this benchmark.

content_consumed.note: With PRISM, no source files were read directly. All context came from PRISM task/search/brief outputs.

token_usage.note: Server-side API token usage metrics are not exposed in the local agent transcript.

tool_calls.note: Equal tool call count in isolated task phases. With PRISM, 4 calls are PRISM-specific (init, task, brief, search) replacing 2 file reads and 2 other calls.

source_content_consumed_chars.note: In the task-only view, with-PRISM consumed more chars (PRISM output is verbose). In a truly isolated run, without-PRISM would need to read full source files (~42120 chars vs ~4876 chars = 88% reduction).

isolated_run_content_estimate.note: This estimates the content token difference in a fully isolated run where both agents start from scratch. The without-PRISM agent must read config.py and agent.py in full to find the bug.

actual_token_comparison.reason: Actual API-level token counts (input_tokens, cached_input_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens) are not accessible from the agent's local transcript. These require API-level metering (e.g., the Anthropic API usage header or billing dashboard). The benchmark cannot report real token savings without this infrastructure.
actual_token_comparison.recommendation: To get actual token counts: (1) Use the API's usage response headers, (2) Use a proxy like LiteLLM that logs token usage, or (3) Run the benchmark through a wrapper that captures API response metadata.

prism_index_cost_per_run.note: PRISM indexing is a one-time cost per repository. The index stays fresh via incremental updates (~0.4s per file change).

1_task.note: Index is zero LLM cost. Context pack is the only overhead.

5_tasks.note: Context cost is per-task, not amortized. Index cost (0 LLM tokens) is already zero.

amortized_cost.note: Since PRISM uses zero LLM tokens for indexing, the amortization only applies to wall-clock time (10s). The per-task context cost (~1220 est. tokens) is constant.

threats_to_validity: CRITICAL: Actual API token counts are not available. All token estimates use chars/4 approximation.
Both runs executed within the same conversation context (shared system prompt, growing context window), not in truly isolated agent sessions.
The task was performed by the same agent sequentially, not by separate fresh agents — context from the first run may have aided the second.
The without-PRISM run benefited from shared setup that read config.py and agent.py before the task began. A truly isolated without-PRISM agent would consume significantly more tokens.
No prompt hook was used — PRISM CLI was called manually. A prompt-hook integration would inject context automatically at session start.
This is a single task on a small repository (8 Python files). PRISM's advantages grow with repository size.
The benchmark was not rate-limited or interrupted.
The model used is Claude Opus 4.6 (Thinking). Results may differ with other models.

confidence_limits.correctness: HIGH — Both runs produce identical, correct fixes verified by 7 deterministic test cases.
confidence_limits.content_token_savings: MEDIUM — Estimated at 88% content token reduction for isolated runs, based on chars/4 approximation, not actual tokenizer counts.
confidence_limits.elapsed_time_savings: LOW — 19.8% time saving observed, but single-run measurement with no statistical significance.
confidence_limits.actual_api_token_savings: NOT_MEASURABLE — API-level token counts are not accessible from within the agent runtime.
